rename(iris, !!! setNames("Petal.Length", "petal_length"))

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Hadley! That is convenient when there is one variable to rename. Needed to flip the order of the strings for it to work with the iris dataset:

rename(iris, !!"petal_length" := !!"Petal.Length")

I was hoping the same approach would work with filter. However, the following doesn't work:

filter(iris, !! "Species" == "setosa")

However, these do work:

filter(iris, .data[["Species"]] == "setosa")

filter(iris, (!! sym("Species")) == "setosa")

messages.subject: Re: dplyr 0.7 in shiny apps: Will "_" versions of verbs really be removed from dplyr?
messages.subject_clean: dplyr 0.7 in shiny apps: Will "_" versions of verbs really be removed from dplyr?
messages.body_plain:
On Fri, Jul 7, 2017 at 7:24 PM, Vincent <vincen...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Hadley! That is convenient when there is one variable to rename.
> Needed to flip the order of the strings for it to work with the iris
> dataset:
>
> rename(iris, !!"petal_length" := !!"Petal.Length")
>
> I was hoping the same approach would work with filter. However, the
> following doesn't work:
>
> filter(iris, !! "Species" == "setosa")

This doesn't work for two reasons:

* !! on the LHS of := has special behaviour because the LHS of an =
must be a name (so we can safely coerce a string)

* !! on the RHS works in select (but not elsewhere) because select()
can take column names as strings.

Hadley

--
http://hadley.nz

messages.subject: Re: elegant way to find-and-replace?
messages.body_plain:
I would try using the str_replace or str_replace_all  from the stringr package with a mutate call like this:

This allows you to mutate, or operate on the column, by essentially overwriting the column with a new copy of it, and saving your new data in 'newdata'. Let me know if you have questions.

newdata <- data %>%
  mutate(col1 = str_replace_all(col1, "-999",""))

On Wednesday, June 21, 2017 at 7:27:30 PM UTC-5, Daniel Nidzgorski wrote:
> I often have data where I need to find-and-replace specified values within a column, leaving other values intact. I've been using the standard base-R methods below, which work, but it seems like there should be a more elegant solution. I've been looking within the tidyverse (especially dplyr) and can't find anything that does this.
>
> As an example, let's say that I want to find and replace all instances in the data where a temperature logger has returned its error code of -999:
>
> data<-tibble(temperature=c(1,3,5,2,-999,2,3,2,-999,4,5))
>
> I could use either:
> data$temperature<-ifelse(data$temperature == -999, NA, data$temperature)
> or else:
> df$temperature<-replace(df$temperature, df$temperature == -999, NA)
>
> The above code produces the result I want, but it's clunkier than it ought to be. I'm looking for a solution that's more straightforward, without repeating data$temperature so many times. I'm envisioning something like this hypothetical function:
> data<-data %>%
>  find_replace(temperature,-999,NA)
>
> If an elegant solution exists, I'd appreciate someone pointing me to it -- thanks!
>
> Best,
> Daniel
>

messages.body_plain:
Here is my code:

pacman::p_load(tibble, stringr, dplyr, readr)
#Create Data
dataa<-tibble(temperature=c(1,3,5,2,-999,2,3,2,-999,4,5))
#Convert column to string to work with
dataa$temperature <- as.character(dataa$temperature)
str(dataa)

##Replace -999 with NA and put the results into a new df
dataa2<- dataa %>%
   mutate(temperature = str_replace_all(temperature, "-999", "NA"))

str(dataa)
#Inspect new dataframe
  dataa2$temperature <- as.numeric(dataa2$temperature)
str(dataa2)

I would be interested in how to convert objects within piping sequence, as I had some issues with

Error in function_list[[i]](value) : object '' not found r
but I think the general strategy is to read in the columns as character vectors, cleanup the data, and then coerce it to your correct data type for calculating on, if that makes sense. Let me know what you thoughts are on this code.

messages.subject: summarize_all() and approx()
messages.body_plain:
Dear all

I'm trying to get summarize_all() to work with approx(). More concrete,
the data frame df is to be interpolated to height_target:

library(tidyverse)
df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
             a = c(1, 3, 5),
             b = c(4, 6, 8))
height_target <- c(5, 15)

For the a column, the commands works like this:

approx(x = df$height, y = df$a, xout = height_target)

I was able to wrap it with summarize, which produces what I want but
only for one column:

summarize(df, h = list(height_target)
       a = list(approx(x = height, y = a, xout = height_target)$y)) %>%
  unnest()

To apply it to all columns, I would do something like

summarize_all(df,
   funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))
)

This, however, gives the error
> Error in summarise_impl(.data, dots) :
>  Evaluation error: 'x' and 'y' lengths differ.

Could you please point me to the error?

Thanks a lot
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: summarize_all() and approx()
messages.body_plain:
Using `.` in place of y is throwing an error because `.` is a dataframe and not the same length as .$height. This error makes sense, but I don't know how to get around it.

I couldn't crack it with summarise_all() so I went a different way using purrrrrrr

library(tidyverse)
df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
             a = c(1, 3, 5),
             b = c(4, 6, 8))

height_target <- data.frame(height = c(5, 15)) # put this in a dataframe with the label height for predict later

gather(df, type, value, -height) %>%  # gather up the different columns that you want to summarize
group_by(type) %>%   # groupt by the type
nest(-type, .key = data) %>%  # nest these datasets, but keep the label type
mutate(model = map(data, function(d) lm(value~height, data = d)), # compute the linear model (this is what approx does I believe)
pred = map(model, function(p) data.frame(height = height_target, prediction = predict(p, height_target))) # predict the values for each based upon their linear model at each point in height_target
) %>%
select(type, pred) %>% # select out these columns because they are compatible lengths for unnest()
unnest() # unwind everything again, you have type, height value from height_target, and predicted value at each target

Hopefully the steps are explained well enough in comments. I'm only just getting my head around map and its kin so there may be a way more efficient way to do this, but I couldn't come up with a way to use approx without the name of the column.

HTH,

B

Actually, I am not sure whether this is correct. I tested this with this:

df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
             a = c(1, 3, 5),
             b = c(4, 6, 8))

summarize_all(df, funs(length(.)))
# # A tibble: 1 x 3
#   height     a     b
#    <int> <int> <int>
# 1      3     3     3

 dfs <- summarize_all(df, funs(list(.)))
dfs$height
# [[1]]
# [1]  0 10 20
dfs$a
# [[1]]
# [1] 1 3 5
dfs$b
# [[1]]
# [1] 4 6 8

For me, it looks like '.' is really a single column. Thus, I am not
really sure whether the error

> Error in summarise_impl(.data, dots) :
>  Evaluation error: 'x' and 'y' lengths differ.

of the command

summarize_all(df,
        funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))
)
